steps.title: Step 1. Value per gallon
lines: Savings per gallon = ND clear tax − ND dyed tax = 23¢ − 4¢ = 19¢.
The 24.4¢ federal tax is not relieved, so it is not counted. Federal revenue forgone = $0.
Price rise = $6.53 − $3.74 = $2.79/gal; 19¢ ÷ $2.79 = 6.8% of the rise on a covered gallon.

steps.title: Step 2. Tons harvested inside the window
lines: Tons in window = production (tons) × share not yet harvested on Sept. 27 × share of the remainder done by Nov. 30.
Soybeans: 6.11M t × 0.78 × 0.994 = 4.74 million t.
Sugarbeets: 5.90M t × 0.75 × 0.987 = 4.36 million t.
Sunflower, dry beans, potatoes (other fall crops) = 1.09 million t.

steps.title: Step 3. Fuel per ton hauled
lines: Gallons per ton = (one-way miles ÷ loaded mpg + one-way miles ÷ empty mpg) ÷ tons per load.
Sugarbeets to station: (11.0 ÷ 5.1 + 11.0 ÷ 6.2) ÷ 21.48 = 0.183 gal/t.

steps.title: Step 4. Category A: hauling the fall harvest = 5.09 million gal
lines: Tons to market = corn 13.77 million × 0.367 + soybeans 4.74 million × 0.597 + other fall crops at the pooled share = 8.35 million t.
To market: 8.35 million t × 0.463 = 3.86 million gal.
Sugarbeets: 4.36 million t × 0.183 = 0.80 million gal.
Into bins: tons not hauled straight from the field (corn 67%, soybeans 40%) = 11.79 million t × 0.036 = 0.43 million gal.
Total A = 5.09 million gal.

steps.title: Step 5. Category B: calves and fertilizer = 0.76 million gal
lines: Calves: 860,000 × 50% ÷ 80 head per load × 80 mi ÷ 6.2 mpg = 0.069 million gal.
Anhydrous: 4.45M ac × 146 lb N ÷ 0.82 ÷ 2,000 = 396k t × 50% ÷ 2.1 t per tank × 55.6 mi ÷ 7.6 mpg = 0.690 million gal.

steps.title: Step 6. Category C: selling stored wheat and barley = 0.39 million gal
lines: Sept. 1–Dec. 1 decline in ND on-farm stocks: wheat 22.1% (2024), 24.0% (2025); barley 6.1% (2024), 33.3% (2025).
Each year's rates × 2026 Sept. 1 stocks (wheat 165M bu at 60 lb, barley 18.5M bu at 48 lb) × 63/91 days, averaged over the two years = 0.85 million t.
0.85 million t × 0.463 gal/t = 0.39 million gal.

steps.title: Step 7. Eligible on-road truck gallons = 6.24 million
lines: A + B + C = 5.09 million + 0.76 million + 0.39 million = 6.24 million gal. Farm pickups are excluded.

steps.title: Step 8. Gallons switched to dyed fuel = 3.18 million
lines: Share switching = fueled from farm tanks 0.528 × staying in ND 0.965 × willing to take federal risk 1.00 = 0.509.
Switched = 6.24 million × 0.509 = 3.18 million gal.

Federal risk: the governor's order covers state penalties only. Until the IRS grants relief, a truck caught with dyed fuel on a public road faces a federal penalty of $1,000 or $10 a gallon, whichever is greater. Assuming every farmer accepts that risk makes this an upper bound on this factor.

steps.title: Step 9. State revenue forgone = $0.60 million
lines: 3.18 million gal × $0.19 = $0.604 million.
Split (NDCC 54-27-19): state highway fund $362K; counties $154K; cities $57K; townships $21K; public transit $10K.

steps.title: Step 10. Context
lines: Fall farm diesel = harvest field work 34.3 million + fall tillage 1.6 million + fall anhydrous 1.2 million + on-road 6.2 million = 43.4 million gal (33% of annual).
Harvest field work by crop: corn 13.0 million; sugarbeets 0.5 million; soybeans 18.3 million; sunflower 1.9 million; dry beans 0.6 million.
Extra cost from price rise = 43.4 million × $2.79 = $121 million; relief ÷ extra cost = 0.50%.
Per farm = $603,546 ÷ 25,068 = $24. Per fall-crop acre = 5.3¢. Per bushel of corn and soybeans harvested in window = 0.093¢.

steps.title: Step 11. Example farm (1,000 ac corn + 1,000 ac soybeans)
lines: Bushels = 1,000 × 130 + 1,000 × 30 = 160,000. Same shares and fuel per ton as Steps 2–4.
On-road truck fuel = 803 gal; savings = 803 × $0.19 = $153.
Higher fall diesel bill = (803 + 5,621) × $2.79 = $17,893.

steps.title: Step 12. Range and cross-check
lines: Each input is moved to its low and high value one at a time. The log changes in switched gallons are combined in quadrature (inputs treated as independent): 2.3 million–4.5 million gal, $0.44–0.85 million. All inputs at their extremes together: $0.20–1.25 million.

Fleet cross-check: 26,227 non-pickup farm trucks × UGPTI annual miles by type ÷ ORNL mpg = 18.4 million gal/yr × 33% of the year's crop tonnage moved in window = 6.1 million gal, vs. 5.1 million gal bottom-up for the same hauls.
